p1s.summary: The journal-name field of every reference entry is read by no gate, and one of the 24 entries is not even covered by the fetch artifact it is supposed to be written from.
p1s.evidence: `aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md`'s own banner says the journal name 'is written from journal-abbreviations.json by journal_abbreviations.py ... re-checked with `--check`'. At the pin `--check` is invoked nowhere: `git grep -n journal_abbreviations f9e5059 -- 'scripts/*' '.github/**'` returns exactly one hit, `.github/workflows/fusion-cpu-extras.yml:2735`, which runs the FETCH (`python research/manuscripts/journal_abbreviations.py`); `scripts/preflight.sh`, `.github/workflows/tests.yml` and `scripts/regenerate_aso_chain.sh` never call it. And `check()` in research/manuscripts/journal_abbreviations.py reads `if not pmid or pmid not in meta: continue` -- a reference whose PMID has no fetched record is skipped silently, not reported. `aso/journal-abbreviations.json` carries `n_entries: 23`, `n_fetched: 23`, `without_fetched_abbreviation: []` while the list holds 24 numbered entries; PMID 41755350 (reference 3, printed journal 'Histopathology') is absent from its `by_pmid`. CORRECT AT THE PIN: PubMed's record for 41755350 gives iso_abbreviation 'Histopathology', which is what the entry prints. CONTRAST, and it is why this is a gap rather than a policy: the AUTHOR segment of the same entries IS bound -- `test_every_entry_names_the_authors_the_venue_asks_for` asserts `unfetched` is empty and would fail on exactly this condition; `journal-reference-authors.json` covers all 24 PMIDs.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Typing, 'correcting' or abbreviating any journal name in fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md, or adding a 25th reference without re-running the CI fetch. Every gate stays green: lint_citations reads identifiers, not journal names; test_every_entry_is_in_the_style_the_venue_asks_for matches `.+ ` where the journal goes; and journal_abbreviations.py --check is not run and would skip the entry anyway.

p1s.summary: Printed reference numbering is verified in one of the five typeset deliverables; the .docx -- the format the venue prefers -- numbers its references by POSITION, the same mechanism class that once misnumbered two thirds of the citations in a built PDF.
p1s.evidence: `test_the_printed_pdf_numbers_the_references_as_the_prose_cites_them` in test_journal_references_match_the_prose.py opens exactly one file: `aso/fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf`. Nothing reads printed reference numbers in `-manuscript.docx`, `-manuscript.pdf`, `-preprint.pdf` or `-anonymized.pdf` (grep for 'References|printed' across test_pdf_text_layer_is_orderable.py, test_a_display_item_cell_is_not_clipped.py, test_the_word_manuscript_is_current_and_whole.py and test_the_submission_uploads_are_individual_files.py returns no numbering check). The .docx risk is the same one that docstring exists for: read from its bytes, all 24 reference paragraphs in word/document.xml carry `<w:numPr><w:ilvl w:val="0"/><w:numId w:val="1"/></w:numPr>` and NO literal digit, and word/numbering.xml renders numId 1 as `decimal` from `<w:start w:val="1"/>` -- so Word prints 1..N from position exactly as an HTML <ol> does. CORRECT AT THE PIN: the 24 numId=1 paragraphs are the 24 reference entries in markdown order (Labelle 1 ... Lee 24), and all four PDFs print 'N. Surname' for every N in 1..24 with the PMID each superscript names.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Any reordering, insertion or deletion in fusion-junction-aso-journal-references.md that leaves the markdown labels correct but the ORDER wrong -- the historical defect exactly. The markdown tests read labels, the one PDF test would catch it in fusion-junction-aso-journal-article.pdf only, and the .docx an editor opens would silently renumber from 1.

p1s.summary: The two cell-line RRIDs the paper prints are outside lint_citations' identifier classes entirely -- not anchored, not baselined, not counted.
p1s.evidence: `PATTERNS` in research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py at the pin defines PMID, PMCID, DOI, NCT, GEO and ARXIV. There is no RRID/CVCL class, so `USZ20-EMC1 (RRID:CVCL_C6MX)` and `USZ22-EMC2 (RRID:CVCL_C6MY)` in the Results are invisible to the gate whose stated purpose is 'an identifier that exists ONLY in prose has no such origin'. `git grep CVCL` over research/manuscripts/tests/ and research/modalities/tests/ at the pin returns nothing that binds the article to a record; the only manuscript-side hit is a nowrap typesetting regex, build_submission_pdf.py:749. CORRECT AT THE PIN: both RRIDs match a committed Cellosaurus fetch -- aso/fusion-junction-aso-data-sources.json `entries[8].record_id_lines_verbatim` = ['ID H-EMC-SS / AC CVCL_1238', 'ID USZ20-EMC1 / AC CVCL_C6MX', 'ID USZ22-EMC2 / AC CVCL_C6MY'], with api_url_verbatim https://api.cellosaurus.org/search/cell-line -- and research/modalities/emc-model-junction-evidence.json carries the same AC lines per model. ALREADY RECORDED FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION: fusion-junction-aso-guard-coverage-audit.md item 11 swapped the two RRIDs and reports 'both green ... nothing joins the paper to it'. What is added here is that the failure is a missing identifier CLASS, not just a missing binding, so the same hole covers any future RRID in any manuscript.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Swapping the two RRIDs, or mistyping one digit of either. Nothing reads them: lint_citations has no pattern, no test names CVCL, and a wrong RRID sends a laboratory to a different cell line.

p1s.summary: Nothing binds the DOI the paper calls 'the citable record' to whether that DOI is published; at the pin it names a DRAFTED, unpublished Zenodo version.
p1s.evidence: Data availability prints `doi:10.5281/zenodo.22182180` and calls it 'the citable record for them'. aso/deposit-state.json at the pin records that DOI under `pending` (drafted 2026-08-30, supersedes 10.5281/zenodo.22180100); `published.doi` is 10.5281/zenodo.22180100. `test_aso_deposition_doi_is_one_fact.py::test_the_article_prints_the_manifests_doi_and_prints_only_that_one` binds the printed DOI to `manifest.deposition_doi`, which is also 10.5281/zenodo.22182180 -- so the whole manuscripts suite is green over a paper citing a DOI that does not resolve, and no test reads deposit-state.json's published/pending split. WHAT I COULD VERIFY DOES FAIL CLOSED: scripts/zenodo_deposit.py::refuse_unless_publishable exits if `pending.uploaded_manifest_digest` != `manifest.archive_content_digest`, and at the pin those differ (ae840abfaff219fac... uploaded at git b93499e944 vs aa5880ff9ef0e2a1... at manifest git_revision a294fee68f), so a publish today refuses rather than freezing a stale archive -- the documented reserve-then-rebuild window, working. THE OBSERVATION THAT WOULD SETTLE THE OTHER HALF: whether any clause stops the PAPER being posted while the printed DOI is still `pending` -- that lives in research/autonomy/publish_bar.py, which this round may not read.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Posting the paper before act (2)+(3) of deposit-state.json's `_what_remains` (refresh the draft at the final commit, then publish). Every committed gate over the manuscript stays green, and a reader following the printed DOI would get nothing.

p2s.summary: fusion-junction-aso-2026-citation-resolution.json numbers its rows in the EXTENDED report's scheme while describing itself as the check for 'the fusion-junction ASO manuscript'.
p2s.evidence: Its `_why` quotes 'Verify the 2026 citations (refs 3, 22, 33) resolve' and its rows carry `reference_number_in_manuscript` 3, 22 and 33. In the journal article at the pin reference 22 is PMID 36316541 (Bangerter) and there is no reference 33; the file's row 22 is PMID 41614678 (Curr Protoc). Only row 3 (PMID 41755350) coincides. Not in the outgoing set -- a reader of the paper never sees it -- but a next session reading it as the journal article's resolution check gets the wrong mapping.

p2s.summary: The deposit contains three .docx build stamps and zero .docx files.
p2s.evidence: fusion-junction-aso-archive-manifest.json at the pin: `payload_file_types.by_extension` lists .json .py .md .pdf .png .svg .csv .fasta .sh and NO .docx (0 of 515 paths end in .docx), while `promises[26] deposited_documents` includes fusion-junction-aso-journal-article-manuscript.docx.build-stamp.json, -title-page.docx.build-stamp.json and -figure-legends.docx.build-stamp.json. A downloader gets a currency stamp for a file the archive does not carry. The journal article's own Data availability promises 'All code, graded artefacts, per-design tables, every screen's parameters and the complete bounds on each claim' and does not promise the .docx, so no promise this paper makes is broken.

p2s.summary: The Introduction describes the cited 2025 industry recommendations as 'five steps, the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory'; two of the five are not laboratory steps in the source's own words.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript, Introduction: 'An industry working group's 2025 off-target recommendations<sup>14</sup> set five steps, the first in silico and the rest in the laboratory.' PMID 39912803's abstract, retrieved from PubMed: 'The proposed workflow encompasses five key steps: (1) OffT identification through complementarity prediction and transcriptomics analysis, (2) focus on cell types with relevant ONT activity, (3) verification and margin assessment, (4) risk assessment based on the OffT biological role, and (5) management of unavoidable OffTs.' Steps 4 and 5 are assessment and mitigation, not laboratory work. The load-bearing halves are accurate and unaffected: step 1 has an in-silico component, which is the half this work performs and stops at, and step 3 is the margin measurement the Discussion specifies. Settled by the framework's own workflow figure in the full text, which is not open access.
